rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-six builder trees go (a row of queen palms and corals every 6-10 m along the back fences, magnolias crowded by the seating, others in the yards); seven come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the picnic table, the grills, the chairs, on the open lot corner.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 13 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the big open lot corner, 35 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the west back yard with the kettle grill and the beach umbrella: a magnolia over both
the next yard's adirondack chair and umbrella, 28 m on: the same
the yard with the adirondack chair and the gas grill: a jacaranda over them
the south-west yard with the two white adirondack chairs: shade for them
